t: The Fourth Republic of Ghana was inaugurated with Jerry Rawlings, the country's former military ruler, as president.
The Braer Storm, the strongest extratropical cyclone ever recorded in the North Atlantic, reached peak intensity.
The first version of Mosaic, created by Marc Andreessen and Eric Bina, was released, becoming the first popular web browser.
Pakistani national Mir Aimal Kansi shot five people outside the Central Intelligence Agency headquarters in Langley, Virginia, killing two.
Two-year-old James Bulger was led away from New Strand Shopping Centre in Bootle, England, and murdered by two 10-year-old boys, who became the youngest convicted murderers in modern English history.
The U.S. Senate unanimously confirmed Janet Reno as the first female United States attorney general.
The Troubles: Two children were killed by the second of two bomb attacks by the Provisional Irish Republican Army in Warrington, England.
The demolition of Kowloon Walled City, a densely crowded slum in Hong Kong, began.
Jiang Zemin succeeded Yang Shangkun to become President of the People's Republic of China.
Iranian filmmaker Morteza Avini was killed by a land mine in Fakkeh while producing a documentary.
Prisoners at the Southern Ohio Correctional Facility near Lucasville, Ohio, rioted and took over the prison for 11 days, resulting in the deaths of one officer and nine inmates.
Bosnian War: NATO forces began Operation Deny Flight to enforce a no-fly zone over Bosnia and Herzegovina ordered by the United Nations Security Council.

Stephen Lawrence, a black British teenager, was murdered while waiting for a bus in Eltham, London, leading to cultural changes of attitudes on racism and the police, and to the law and police practice.

The Provisional Irish Republican Army detonated a truck bomb in London's financial district in Bishopsgate, killing one person, injuring forty-four others, and causing damage that cost £350 million to repair.
Thirty people died, including players and staff of the Zambia football team and the crew, in a plane crash en route to play a World Cup qualifying match against Senegal.
"One for the Road", the series finale of American television sitcom Cheers, was watched by 42.4 million American households on its original airing.
Asiana Airlines Flight 733 crashed into a mountain during a failed attempt to land at Mokpo Airport, South Korea, leading to the deaths of 68 people on board.
Wizards of the Coast released Magic: The Gathering, the first trading card game.
The NASA spacecraft Galileo flew by the asteroid 243 Ida and took photographs that later revealed the first known asteroid moon.
The NASA spacecraft Galileo flew by the asteroid 243 Ida and took photographs that later revealed the first known asteroid moon.
Nirvana released their third and final studio album, In Utero, which went on to sell more than 15 million copies.

A tugboat towing a barge collided with a rail bridge in Mobile, Alabama, U.S., deforming the tracks and causing the derailment of a passenger train eight minutes later, which killed 47 people and injured an additional 103.
Norodom Sihanouk became King of Cambodia with the restoration of the monarchy after a 23-year interregnum.
Nihilism, the first professional runway show from the British designer Alexander McQueen, was staged in London.
Widerøe Flight 744 suffered a controlled flight into terrain while on approach to Namsos Airport, Norway, killing two crew members and four passengers.
The Troubles: Three members of the Ulster Defence Association opened fire in a crowded pub during a Halloween party, killing eight people and wounding nineteen others.
Bosnian War: Croatian Defence Council forces destroyed the Stari Most, a 16th-century bridge crossing the river Neretva in the city of Mostar.
The video game Doom, later considered the "father" of the first-person shooter genre, is released.
Brandon Teena, an American trans man, was raped and murdered in Humboldt, Nebraska; his death led to increased lobbying for hate crime laws in the United States.
